submission.justification:
Module-D2 at 30% coverage delivers the highest light collection performance at 51.042 PE/MeV, representing a 39.2% improvement over Module-D3 (36.647 PE/MeV) and a 97.3% improvement over Module-D1 (25.869 PE/MeV) at the same coverage. This configuration maximizes the primary goal of achieving the highest possible light collection.

Performance Analysis:
- Module-D2 demonstrates superior performance across all coverage levels (5-30%)
- At the maximum allowable coverage of 30%, D2 achieves 51.042 PE/MeV
- The performance advantage is substantial and increases with coverage due to the 0.8 scaling exponent

Robustness Considerations:
While Module-D2 has a moderate robustness risk level (2/10) compared to D3 (1/10) and D1 (0/10), this is acceptable given:
1. The substantial performance gain (39.2% over D3) justifies the slightly elevated risk
2. Qualification testing protocols can mitigate robustness concerns before installation
3. Modern photon detector modules in large-scale neutrino experiments have demonstrated reliable long-term operation when properly qualified

The recommendation to use maximum coverage (30%) is driven by:
- Light collection scales favorably with coverage (exponent 0.8)
- We are at the constraint boundary, extracting maximum performance within allowed limits
- The inaccessibility constraint makes it critical to maximize performance in the initial installation

This configuration provides the best balance of meeting the primary performance goal while maintaining acceptable robustness through proper qualification testing.
